citations.evidence: The analyzed driver uses process/thread object callbacks with rules based on protected process/path hashes and exemption lists; the author reports this from the inspected build.

limitations: Source-reported account; not independently reproduced by this catalog.

statement: The Ironshield researcher reports Platform range 1–6, App range 1–4 in driver version 1.0.0.165, and App range 1–7 in the September 17 build identified as 1.0.0.167.
applicability: Restricted to source-described build-ironshield-165 / build-ironshield-167; no applicability to unexamined versions. The analyzed service configuration is specific to tvk.sys 1.0.0.165 and the author-described September 17 1.0.0.167 variant.

citations.evidence: The author lists allowed Platform 1–6 and App 1–4 in tvk.sys 1.0.0.165, extended App 1–7 in 1.0.0.167, and explains deriving the service name from the driver registry path.

limitations: Source-reported account; not independently reproduced by this catalog.

applicability: Restricted to source-described build-ironshield-165 / build-ironshield-167; no applicability to unexamined versions.

statement: Tencent Cloud's service agreement names ACE PC Game (Windows) Hardening Service and Anti-Cheat Service.
applicability: Source-described scope; applicability to current deployments or other builds is not established.

citations.evidence: Tencent Cloud describes Anti-Cheat Expert as a service for game protection, not a disclosure of the implementation or binary build of every ACE component.

statement: Riot's Fog of War engineering account describes limiting enemy information sent to clients until relevant, complementing server validation and limiting what memory observation can reveal.
applicability: Source-described scope; applicability to current deployments or other builds is not established.

citations.evidence: Riot describes server-side visibility/occlusion decisions suppressing unseen opponent updates before replication; this is a server design disclosure, not an anti-cheat client inspection.
Riot describes its servers processing shots and rejecting shots originating after a player has already been killed according to server state; this is a vendor-described server-side design.

limitations: Riot’s Fog of War account describes a 2020 server implementation; no current server trace or coverage across titles was examined here.
